summary:
NOT VERIFIED IN THE REAL GAME: nothing here ran in the real client or against a server. The real HUD was mounted over the dev page scene 'surface' by a scratch script with a stand-in for the game core, and that is the only place it was rendered. Six things were seen only with forced or fake data, because the scene cannot produce them: the gravity warning (the scene's body pulls 0.69 m/s² against 21.8 m/s² of lift, so I forced the lift to 0.3), the cruise-drop prompt (view forced to cruise), the notices (pushed into the store), the base's station panel, the docked text and the destroyed screen (fake pilot and station data). The last rule change (cues hidden while climbing away below 50 m) was unit-tested and typechecked but not rendered again, and the client was not rebuilt after it.

What is now true in packages/client: near a landable body the HUD shows height above ground, sink or climb rate and ground speed in a row above the speed readout; in the last seconds before a touchdown those cells show the shared landing limits behind the values, slope and tilt appear left and right of the speed, and whatever is exceeded turns red with a line that names it; a landed ship shows a boxed LANDED in the mode line and a lift-off prompt; a body that pulls harder than the vertical thrusters push at the present engine power gives a warning from the surface-frame height down; the ground and cruise notices and five refusals appear in the pilot's language; ground bases have their own label in the navigation list, a marker from anywhere in the system, their own wording in the station panel, the docked line and the respawn button; key line and help text explain landing and lift-off; every new string exists in English and German, and a test now fails if German lacks a key or a placeholder.

Decided as asked: the cruise-drop prompt for a base now needs three things: ship below the surface-frame height of the base's body, ship above the horizon of the pad, base within 100 km. Only the prompt changed; I did not read or change what the J key does.

Final checks: three typechecks clean, 38 test files, 587 passed plus 2 expected-fail (not in my file). I did not read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (the owner's budget note limited reading to the HUD files, reports and constants) and did not run npm run build or scripts/e2e.mjs. For the 95 % rule: when I finished, the usage meter read 92 % weekly Fable and 63 % of the 5-hour limit, so I sent no push.
behaviour:
GROUND ROW (Hud.tsx, flightHud). Shown whenever view.surface.ship exists and the ship is not landed, in normal flight and in cruise, so anywhere within 3 radii of a landable body (also at a station that close to one). Three fixed-width cells above the speed readout: height above ground, sink or climb rate, ground speed. Height (format.ts fmtHeight): below 19.95 m one decimal in metres, below 999.5 m whole metres, below 99,995 m kilometres with two decimals, below 999,950 m one decimal, above that whole kilometres. Vertical: label SINK RATE unless the ship climbs at 0.05 m/s or more, then CLIMB RATE; the number is the magnitude, one decimal below 100 m/s. While ground data is present the centre block stands on a dark plate (rgba 6,14,28 at 0.72).

LANDING CUES (landing.ts). A landing is near when the ship is in normal flight and either below 50 m and not climbing faster than 1 m/s, or sinking with the ground less than 15 s away at the present sink rate. Then sink rate and ground speed show as value / limit against LAND_MAX_SINK (6 m/s) and LAND_MAX_SIDE (8 m/s), and slope and tilt appear left and right of the speed against LAND_MAX_SLOPE_DEG (20) and LAND_MAX_TILT_DEG (30). All four are imported, none copied. They are measured as the simulation's ground contact measures them: velocity split along the ground normal (self.vel against surface.ship.normal), slope from surface.ship.slope, tilt as the angle between the ship's up axis (self.rot) and the normal. A cell is calm until value > limit, then its label and number turn red and a red line above the row names it: SINK RATE TOO HIGH, GROUND SPEED TOO HIGH, SLOPE TOO STEEP TO LAND, SHIP TILTED TOO FAR. The 'sideways' limit is worded as ground speed because the simulation applies it to speed along the ground in every direction, forward included.

LANDED. Mode line shows a boxed cyan LANDED / GELANDET instead of NORMAL FLIGHT, the ground row is gone, a prompt says 'Press Space to lift off' (the key comes from the thrustUp binding), and the dock prompt follows when a base is within reach.

KEY LINE. Landed: 'Space lift off · F dock at a base · M map · N nav · V camera · Esc menu'. Normal flight below 2,000 m above ground: 'Land: descend gently with Ctrl or C · the ship settles by itself · Space climb · F dock at a base'. Otherwise the old line. The line now wraps inside the bottom right corner (max-width 30vw, balanced).

GRAVITY (landing.ts liftBalance). Surface gravity G * mass / radius² of the body against stats.accelVert * engineMul(pips). When gravity is larger and the ship's centre distance is below the surface-frame height of that body (60 to 300 km up): in normal flight and in cruise the red warning 'HIGH GRAVITY g m/s² · VERTICAL THRUST ONLY x m/s²' among the other warnings for as long as it holds; landed, the same words in amber under the mode line. Boost is not counted.

CRUISE-DROP PROMPT FOR A BASE (landing.ts baseDropHere). In cruise with a ground base as nav target: ship centre distance below BodySurface.enter of the base's body, AND dot(ship - pad, pad) >= 0 in body-fixed axes (ship above the horizon plane of the pad, terrain ignored), AND straight-line distance to the pad at most BASE_DROP_RANGE = 100,000 m. Line of sight alone is not enough: from 60 km over a 1,336 km body the horizon is 405 km away, 26 minutes at 260 m/s. 100 km is about 5 minutes for the fastest hull (330 m/s) and 9 for the slowest (185 m/s). Orbital sites keep the old rule (distance below the site's frame radius).

NOTICES (landing.ts noticeKey). By code: cruise_ceiling, cruise_ground, cruise_masslock, charge_landed, crash. Refused commands arrive with the code 'refused' and only the server's English sentence, so five are matched by that exact sentence: 'Lift off first.', 'Too close to the ground: climb above the cruise ceiling.', 'Mass-locked: move away from the structure.', 'No base here.', 'Too far from the base.'. Anything else is shown as the server sent it.

SITE KINDS. kind.base = 'Ground base' / 'Bodenbasis' (the navigation list showed the raw key before). HUD marker: bases are marked from anywhere in the system like stations, outposts and gates. Station panel at a base: a line 'Ground base on <body>' under the name, button 'Launch' / 'Starten' instead of 'Undock', 'This base has no market data yet.', 'Foreign cargo this base does not trade'. Docked with the panel closed: 'DOCKED · GROUND BASE'. Destroyed screen: 'Return to your home base' when the home site is a base in the system the pilot died in, otherwise the old text. Galaxy map: the count that includes bases now reads 'Stations and bases: n'.

OTHER CHANGES THAT REACH BEYOND LANDING. Throttle and charge bars have a fixed width of 18em instead of the width of the centre block. The mode line aligns on the text baseline. Space has a key name ('Space' / 'Leertaste') wherever a binding is named. The existing English value of map.stations changed.

verification:
COMMANDS, final tree (commit 7591bbb by the checkpoint job; working tree clean except scripts/e2e.mjs, which is not mine): `npx tsc -p packages/shared && npx tsc -p packages/server && npx tsc -p packages/client` exit 0. `npx vitest run`: 38 files, 587 passed, 2 expected fail (neither in my file). `npx vitest run packages/client/src/ui/landing.test.ts`: 15 passed. Client build: `npx vite build --outDir <scratch>` in packages/client exit 0, run before the last landing.ts change, not after.

RENDERING. Vite dev server on my own port 5311 (--strictPort), stopped afterwards by PID 62824; ports 8420/8421 and .data untouched. shots.mjs loads /dev/local.html?scene=surface&info=0 in headless Chromium at 1280x720, imports the fonts, the store and ui/index.tsx from the dev server, mounts the real interface with a stand-in api (view = window.__view, project copied from Game.ts) and bumps the frame signal. Last full run: 32 shots (16 cases, two languages), no console or page error in any; three more cases (base panel, docked line, destroyed screen) in two languages afterwards, also without errors. Box overlaps were measured with getBoundingClientRect between HUD blocks, ground cells, prompts, mode line, key line, chat lines and marker labels.

THE TEN REQUIRED SCREENSHOTS, final versions, each opened with Read:
- 5km-en / 5km-de: 'HEIGHT ABOVE GROUND 5.00 km | SINK RATE 0.0 m/s | GROUND SPEED 120 m/s' ('HÖHE ÜBER GRUND 5,00 km | SINKRATE 0,0 m/s | FAHRT ÜBER GRUND 120 m/s') on a dark plate above the big 120 m/s, mode line below, general key line in two lines bottom right. No overlap measured. The base marker diamond is cut by the bottom edge of the screen (the base is straight below).
- 300m-en / 300m-de: height '300 m', level flight so no limits shown, dock prompt, key line switched to the landing hints.
- 20m-fast-en / 20m-fast-de (captured at 18.4 to 18.6 m, readout '20 m', sinking 12 m/s): red line 'SINK RATE TOO HIGH' / 'SINKRATE ZU HOCH', sink cell red '12.0 / 6 m/s', ground speed '3.0 / 8 m/s' calm, slope '0.0° / 20°' left and tilt '0.0° / 30°' right of '12 m/s'. The top edge of the plate touches the lower edge of the own ship in the chase view.
- slope-en / slope-de (ground found by scanning the real terrain for 23 to 32 degrees; the view reports 23.68): red line 'SLOPE TOO STEEP TO LAND' / 'HANGNEIGUNG ZU STEIL ZUM LANDEN', slope cell red '23.7° / 20°', tilt '23.7° / 30°' calm.
- landed-en / landed-de: '0 m/s', boxed 'LANDED' / 'GELANDET' beside ASSIST, prompts 'Press Space to lift off' / 'Leertaste drücken zum Abheben' and the dock prompt, short key line in one line.

ALSO OPENED: 20m-chat-en from the run before the plate was added (four long chat lines end 60 px left of the cluster; the last run measured no overlap for the same case), 300m-sinking-de (two red lines; the plate covers the lower third of the own ship), tilt-de (38,0° / 30° red, 'SCHRÄGLAGE ZU GROSS'), cruise-drop-en and -de (forced cruise 36 km from the base at 20 km height: prompt shown, readable on the plate over the sunlit body; without the plate the labels were nearly invisible there, seen in the earlier version), heavy-en (forced lift: red warning at the top), landed-heavy-en (amber line under LANDED), notices-de (six notices in German, the unknown refusal 'Not enough fuel.' in English), navlist-de ('Glildok Base · Bodenbasis · 2,5 km' first in the list), help-de (the landing line in the controls list), base-panel-de ('Bodenbasis auf Craukono VIII b', 'Starten', 'Diese Basis hat noch keine Marktdaten.'). Read as text only, not opened: cruise-far (180 km away: no prompt), base-outside ('DOCKED · GROUND BASE' / 'ANGEDOCKT · BODENBASIS'), dead ('Return to your home base' / 'Zurück zur Heimatbasis').

OVERLAPS AND CLIPPING SEEN AT 1280x720: (1) with the base as nav target straight below the ship, its amber marker label lies over the mode line (notices shots; the marker is clamped to the bottom margin); (2) marker labels are cut at the screen edge (cruise-drop shots, and the diamond in the 5 km shots); both come from the marker code as it was, and a base below the ship makes them common. (3) The plate covers the lower part of the own ship in the chase view when two red lines and a prompt stand together, and touches it with one. Nothing else overlapped in the 32 measured shots, and no text was wider than its cell.

UNIT TESTS cover what the scene cannot show: cue values and limits including a 30 degree slope and the exact limits, the near rule, lift at 0, 4 and 8 engine pips, the drop rule (over the base, above the frame height, far side, below the horizon at 70 km, in sight but 150 km away), the notice table, the height format in both languages.
